verseContext: Paul writes this to a church that was trying very hard to be good by following rules instead of trusting Jesus.
title: The Spirit Grows Good Fruit
subtitle: You cannot squeeze an apple out of a branch — it has to grow
mainTruth: Good fruit is grown by God's Spirit inside us, not manufactured by trying harder. Our job is to stay joined to Jesus.

read.title: Read Together
read.text:
Have you ever seen an apple tree straining? Have you ever heard a branch grunting and puffing, trying really hard to make an apple?

Of course not. Branches do not make fruit by trying. Fruit grows, quietly, because the branch is joined to the tree and the life of the tree flows into it.

Jesus said: 'I am the vine. You are the branches. Stay joined to Me, and you will grow lots of fruit. On your own, you can do nothing.'

And Paul wrote a list of what grows on a person who has God's Spirit living in them. It is one of the loveliest lists in the Bible: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control.

Read that again slowly. Is any of it about being clever, or fast, or good at things? No. It is all about what you are like to be with.

Now here is the part that matters most, and it is easy to get backwards. Paul does not say 'try very hard and produce these nine things.' He calls it fruit — fruit of the Spirit. It grows. God grows it, inside you, over time.

That is such good news for a child who has already tried to be patient and failed by breakfast. You do not have to squeeze it out of yourself. Nobody can.

So what do we do? We stay joined. We talk to God. We listen to His words. We spend time with His people. We say sorry and come back when we wander off — like David did, like Peter did. And the fruit grows, slowly, the way fruit does. You will probably not notice it. Other people will.

Remember the promise the prophets made, long ago, about new hearts and God's own Spirit put inside His people? This is what that looks like when it has been growing for a while.

Branches do not make fruit by trying. Fruit grows quietly, because the branch is joined to the tree. Jesus said, 'I am the vine and you are the branches. Stay joined to Me and you will grow lots of fruit. On your own you can do nothing.' And Paul made a list of what grows on a person who has God's Spirit inside them: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness and self-control. Notice that none of it is about being clever or fast or best. It is all about what you are like to be with. And here is the best part — it is called fruit because it GROWS. God grows it in you. You do not have to squeeze it out of yourself, because nobody can. Our job is just to stay joined to Jesus.

discuss.title: Talk About It
discuss.question: Does a branch have to try hard to grow fruit?
discuss.parentGuide: This is World 9's capstone and the anti-moralism story of the whole app, so guard it carefully. The new concept is sanctification, and the single thing to protect is the word fruit: it grows, God grows it, and it is not a nine-item checklist for a child to achieve. If your child leaves this thinking they must try harder to be patient, the story has taught the opposite of what it says. The branch image does the work — let them tell you what a straining apple tree would look like and enjoy how silly it is. Then be practical about what staying joined actually means: talking to God, hearing His words, being with His people, and coming back when we wander. Retrieve The Prophets Promise New Hearts — this is that promise grown up. It is also worth saying that you will usually not notice your own fruit; other people will, which is a relief rather than a disappointment.
discuss.familyQuestion: Which fruit would our family most like God to grow?

pray.title: Let's Pray
pray.guidedPrayer: Jesus, You are the vine and we are the branches. We cannot make good fruit by ourselves. Please keep us joined to You, and grow Your fruit in us. Amen.
pray.childPrompt: Which fruit would you like God to grow in you?
prayerPoints: Ask God to grow one particular fruit in you
Thank God that He does the growing, so you do not have to squeeze

remember.title: Remember This
remember.memoryVerse: God's Spirit grows love, joy, peace and kindness in us.
remember.tip: Curl up small like a seed on the floor, then grow slowly up onto tiptoes with your arms out like branches, saying: 'God grows good fruit.'

doToday.title: Do It Today
doToday.action: Eat a piece of fruit today, and while you eat it name one fruit of the Spirit you would like God to grow in you.
doToday.parentNote: Name yours too, honestly — patience or gentleness is usually the true answer for a grown-up, and hearing you admit it teaches more than the list does.
